title: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Salary: A Guide for Product Manager Salary
description: Learn how to convert an hourly rate to annual salary using 38-hour weeks. Includes product manager salary benchmarks, National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, and super.
salarySummary: Annual salary is hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours per week times 52 weeks, giving a gross figure before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual salary before tax and super. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, the annual salary is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,257.44 (rounded). The Fair Work Commission states the weekly rate is $1,004.90, so $1,004.90 × 52 = $52,254.80 – a small rounding difference.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and an award rate?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026) is the legal minimum for award/agreement-free employees. Award rates are set by the Fair Work Commission for specific industries and occupations, and are often higher. For example, a product manager may be covered by the Professional Employees Award or another award, which sets a higher minimum rate. Use the Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guides to find the correct award rate for your job. If no award applies, the National Minimum Wage is the floor.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour. When using our calculator, you can check the 'casual loading' box to add this automatically. Note: the loading is applied to the base rate, so do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading. Superannuation is paid on the casual rate as well.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly Rate and Annual Salary

Whether you are negotiating a new role or checking your current pay, converting an hourly rate to an annual salary is a straightforward calculation. For a full-time employee working the standard 38-hour week, the formula is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 = gross annual salary**

This gives you the amount before tax, Medicare levy, and superannuation. It assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For a product manager salary, this conversion helps you compare job offers or benchmark against industry data.

### From Hourly to Annual: The Simple Calculation

Let’s use the National Minimum Wage (NMW) as an example. From 1 July 2026, the NMW is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, or $1,004.90 per week. Multiplying by 52 weeks gives an annual salary of $52,254.80. The fortnightly pay would be $2,009.80 (weekly × 2).

If you are a casual employee, the 25% casual loading applies, making the minimum casual rate $33.05 per hour. The same formula applies: $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,318.80 per year. Remember, superannuation is paid on top of these amounts.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or enterprise agreement. However, many roles – including product managers – are covered by industry-specific awards that set higher minimum rates. For example, the Professional Employees Award or the Clerks Award may apply depending on your duties. Award rates are updated annually and can be found in the Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/blog).

If you are award-free, the NMW is your minimum. But a typical product manager salary is well above the NMW. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings for May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week, which annualises to about $108,352.40. This is a useful benchmark for a mid-level product manager salary, though actual figures vary by industry, experience, and location.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on their base rate. When using our [timesheet](/), you can check the ‘casual loading’ box to automatically add this. Do not enter a rate that already includes the loading – the calculator applies it for you.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For example, if your annual salary is $100,000, your employer must pay an additional $12,000 into your super fund. This is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra cost for the employer.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your gross annual salary is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) applies progressive tax rates for 2026–27:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income over $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low-income earners). Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool to estimate your net pay after tax and Medicare.

### Using the Calculator

Our [timesheet](/) (the home page) lets you enter your base hourly rate. The calculator shows your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay, plus super and estimated tax. It assumes a 38-hour week unless you change the hours. Remember the disclaimer: this is an estimate only, not a determination of your actual pay or tax.

### Product Manager Salary Benchmarks

While the NMW is $26.44 per hour, a product manager salary typically ranges from $90,000 to $130,000 per year, depending on seniority and industry. The ABS figure of $2,083.70 per week ($108,352 annually) is a useful midpoint. To convert a product manager salary offer to an hourly rate, divide the annual salary by 52 weeks and then by 38 hours. For example, a $110,000 salary equals $110,000 ÷ 52 ÷ 38 = $55.66 per hour.

If you are a casual product manager, remember the 25% loading applies on top of the base rate. So a casual rate of $55.66 per hour would actually be $69.58 per hour including loading. Check your award or agreement to confirm your correct classification.

### Summary

Converting your hourly rate to an annual salary is simple: multiply by hours per week and 52. But understanding the difference between the National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, and super is essential to ensure you are paid correctly. For a product manager salary, use the ABS benchmark and your specific award to negotiate confidently. Always refer to the Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/blog) and the Fair Work Commission’s annual wage review for the most current rates.

For a personalised calculation, visit our [the timesheet](/) and enter your details. You can also explore [average pay](/topics/average-pay) and [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) for more insights.
